cohort: The study participants were women who underwent C-section deliveries in both public and private health facilities in Ghana between 2017 and 2021, as recorded in the District Health Information Management System 2 (DHIMS-2) database.
finding: Ghana exhibits a concerning high C-section rate, driven by factors such as advanced maternal age, higher education, formal employment, and regional healthcare disparities.
mod_finding: The study found that more than half of women had a C-section delivery, with advanced maternal age, higher education, and formal employment increasing the likelihood of C-sections.
